You are analysing a negotiation-agent hackathon repo at /Users/stef/Projects/ehlcodacabana-final (read-only; do not modify files). Python 3.12 venv at .venv; run with `.venv/bin/python`.

Context: our buyer agent negotiates by e-mail with LLM supplier bots. The full e-mail exchange of every session is in logs/sessions/practice/*.json and logs/sessions/sandbox/*.json (inspect one file's structure first: print nested keys to depth 3; find the per-thread message list with `direction`/`from`, `body`, `term_sheets`, `status`, `claims`/`refs` results) and in exports/messages.jsonl (older probe sessions, see exports/README.md).

Task: read every SUPPLIER-written e-mail body across all sessions (practice first, then sandbox) and extract:
1. Every explicit ask or question the supplier put to us ("could you confirm the volume", "would you consider 14-day payment", "we would need a 24-month commitment", "send us the forecast", "what is your target"). Count how often each type appears, and check against OUR next e-mail in the same thread whether we answered it (our bodies are the other direction). Table: ask type, count, answered by us (count), example case/supplier.
2. Every explicit trade the supplier offered or hinted at ("if you could ..., we could ..."): lever offered, lever requested, case/supplier.
3. Every reason the supplier gave for refusing to move (frozen prices, material index, capacity, management approval, cost of money), with counts.
4. Wording in OUR e-mails that suppliers reacted to negatively or positively (quote their reaction).
5. What a supplier said in the round just before it sent `final_offer` or `walked_away` (the warning signs), per case.
Under 800 words, tables preferred, with case/supplier/session IDs.

addedLines: Artifact: publishes pages on claude.ai; reads claude.ai artifact links. Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

# AGENTS.md

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of
  adding compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current
  requirements. Avoid speculative abstractions, configuration, and
  indirection.
- Grow the system in layers. Start from the smallest version that works end
  to end, and add each new capability on top of a product that already
  works. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns clearly separated.
- Prefer established, well-maintained libraries when they reduce overall
  complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common
  functionality without a clear reason.
- Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own
  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.
- Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap
  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Terse by default: after an action, state what changed in three lines or
  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package

## Rules

  abstractions, configuration or indirection.

  complexity.

- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |

| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

```sh

uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
```

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

# Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
- `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  `urgency`).
- `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.

## sessions

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
| `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
| `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
| `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |

## threads

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
| `should_cost` | `should_cost.csv`, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
| `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
| `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
| `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` |
| `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
| `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
| `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |

## messages

Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
`signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
`backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).

## claims

`type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
`notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
(`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).

cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-stef-Projects-ehlcodacabana-final/daf2a093-2bd0-4ce9-80b9-341ae1b7774e/scratchpad && cat > warn.py <<'EOF'
import json,collections,re
recs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('corpus.jsonl')]
threads=collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in recs:
    if r['dir']=='SUP' or (r['dir']=='BUY' and r['sup']):
        threads[(r['session'],r['sup'])].append(r)
rows=[]
for key,msgs in threads.items():
    sups=[m for m in msgs if m['dir']=='SUP']
    if not sups: continue
    fin=[m for m in sups if m['status'] in('final_offer','walked_away')]
    last=sups[-1]['status']
    if not fin and last!='agreed': outcome='open-end:'+last
    if fin:
        first=fin[0]
        # previous supplier message
        idx=sups.index(first)
        prev=sups[idx-1] if idx>0 else None
        # our message between prev and first
        ours=[m for m in msgs if prev and m['dir']=='BUY' and m['seq']>prev['seq'] and m['seq']<first['seq']]
        rows.append(dict(case=first['case'],session=key[0][:8],sup=key[1][4:],first=first['status'],round=first['round'],
            prev_status=prev['status'] if prev else None,prev_round=prev['round'] if prev else None,prev_text=(prev['text'] if prev else ''),
            our_between=[o['status'] for o in ours], nfinal=len(fin), ends=sups[-1]['status'], first_text=first['text']))
    else:
        rows.append(dict(case=sups[-1]['case'],session=key[0][:8],sup=key[1][4:],first=None,ends=last))
json.dump(rows,open('warn.json','w'),ensure_ascii=False)
c=collections.Counter((r['case'],r.get('first') or r['ends']) for r in rows)
for k in sorted(c): print(k,c[k])
EOF

    if not sups: continue

    last=sups[-1]['status']
    if not fin and last!='agreed': outcome='open-end:'+last
    if fin:
        first=fin[0]
        # previous supplier message
        idx=sups.index(first)
        prev=sups[idx-1] if idx>0 else None
        # our message between prev and first
        ours=[m for m in msgs if prev and m['dir']=='BUY' and m['seq']>prev['seq'] and m['seq']<first['seq']]
        rows.append(dict(case=first['case'],session=key[0][:8],sup=key[1][4:],first=first['status'],round=first['round'],
            prev_status=prev['status'] if prev else None,prev_round=prev['round'] if prev else None,prev_text=(prev['text'] if prev else ''),
            our_between=[o['status'] for o in ours], nfinal=len(fin), ends=sups[-1]['status'], first_text=first['text']))
    else:
        rows.append(dict(case=sups[-1]['case'],session=key[0][:8],sup=key[1][4:],first=None,ends=last))
json.dump(rows,open('warn.json','w'),ensure_ascii=False)
c=collections.Counter((r['case'],r.get('first') or r['ends']) for r in rows)
for k in sorted(c): print(k,c[k])

import json,re,collections
recs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('corpus.jsonl')]
sup=[r for r in recs if r['dir']=='SUP']
levers={
'OFFERED: faster payment -> lower price':(r'(faster payment|paid faster|getting paid|early payment|\b(\d+)[- ]days? (net )?payment)',r'(reflect|lower|drop|reduce|better price|price (down|lower)|come down|move|meet you|offer|accept|can do|match)'),
'REQUESTED: higher volume for price':(r'(volume)',r'(commit|better price|lower|move|price|higher|bigger|more volume|increase)'),
'REQUESTED: longer contract for price':(r'(longer contract|contract (term|duration)|\d+[- ]month contract|longer-term|longer term|contract commitment|months? contract)',r'(price|lower|competitive|adjust|review|reduce|move|pricing)'),
'REQUESTED: standard/longer lead time for price':(r'(lead ?time|Lieferzeit|delivery time)',r'(price|overtime|premium|push|meet you|drop|cost)'),
'REQUESTED: payment (longer) raises price':(r'(payment|Zahlungsziel)',r'(higher|premium|upwards|increase|financing|adjust the|surcharge)'),
'REQUESTED: ppm / quality for price':(r'(ppm)',r'(price|per unit|chargeback|checks|sorting|cost)'),
'REQUESTED: index clause (drop deadband / fixed price)':(r'(deadband|Preisgleitklausel|index clause|fixed price)',r'(base price|reduce|in return|must|mandatory|cannot)'),
'OFFERED: DAP/incoterm for price':(r'(DAP|incoterm|EXW|FCA|delivery terms?)',r'(per unit|price|offer)'),
'OFFERED: volume/contract for price (their side)':(r'(bigger volume|increase the order volume|more volume|larger volume)',r'(review|talk|pricing|better price|further|move)'),
}
per=collections.defaultdict(lambda: dict(msgs=0,threads=set(),cases=collections.Counter(),ex=None))
for r in sup:

    for line in r['text'].split('\n'):

                    d['ex'] = d['ex'] or (r['case'],r['sup'][4:],s.strip()[:120])
for k,v in levers.items():
    d=per[k]; print(k,'| msgs',d['msgs'],'threads',len(d['threads']),dict(d['cases'].most_common(4)),'| ex',d['ex'])
"

input.message:
Scope: 125 sessions (62 practice, 63 sandbox: D01 48, D02 15, practice P01 to P18). 800 supplier e-mails, 629 of ours, read from the trace in logs/sessions/*/*.json (result.trace; supplier `move.text`, our `move.body`). Counts are e-mails or sentences as noted. Session IDs are the first 8 characters. Scratch scripts are in the scratchpad, not the repo.

**1. Supplier asks**

| Ask | Supplier e-mails (threads) | Our next e-mail | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Which volume can you commit to?" (and "tell me what volume...") | 147 (57) | 23 gave a volume statement, always "our order volume is fixed / full demand, we cannot commit higher"; 97 ignored; 27 no reply | P05 70210 12116e91; D01 DEMO-F1 (76 sentences) |
| Proof of forecast or binding volume ("provide proof of the rising forecast") | 67 (35) | 12 cited a forecast ref; 43 ignored | P02 70510 17a03b8d |
| "Which figures is that based on?" (our should-cost basis) | 19 (19) | 0 answered with a basis; 16 ignored, 3 no reply | P02 70510 17a03b8d; P11 70140 |
| Send data or documents ("please send us the data", "send the 8D report") | 34 (29) | no reply sent the data; our bodies only say "term sheet attached" | P02 70510; P11 70140 |
| Confirm or decide ("please decide", "let me know if we have a deal") | 133 (112) | 108 accept actions in total | D01 DEMO-F1 |
| Payment or lead time question | about 4 | not separately answered | P11 70140 |

**2. Supplier trades** (sentence counts, excluding term lines)

| Lever offered | Lever requested | Sentences (threads) | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lower price for faster payment | Shorter payment (14 days), "faster payment" | payment speed 121 (37) | P11 70140 (65), D02 DEMO-C1 (35), P05 70210 |
| Lower price for higher volume | Higher volume commitment | volume 163 (54) | D01 DEMO-F1 (54), D02 DEMO-C1 (33), P05 70240 |
| Lower price for longer contract | 24 to 36 month contract | contract length 27 (23) | P01 70110 "in exchange for this improved payment term", P03 70530, P07 |
| Lower price for relaxed lead time | Accept 42 or 56 days, or overtime at a premium | lead time 15 (14) | P05 70240 "N days lead time and we drop the price" |
| Lower price for DAP (not EXW) | Our delivery terms | 4 (4) | D02 DEMO-J1 "if you really need DAP delivery" |
| Higher price for tighter ppm (or lower price for looser) | 6400 ppm, chargeback | 9 (7) | P11 70140 "I can come down to N EUR for the N ppm you want, but..." |
| Index clause (drop deadband) | Fixed price over 36 months | 5 (5) | P08 70710 "we are prepared to reduce our base price in return" |

**3. Reasons for not moving** (e-mails, excluding agreed)

| Reason | E-mails (threads) | Main cases |
|---|---|---|
| Cost drivers and indices ("price follows our main cost drivers") | 254 (134) | D01, D02, P08 |
| Our evidence checked, no move ("it holds, but it does not change our calculation") | 137 (91) | D01, P11, D02 |
| Cost breakdown not shared | 154 (126) | D01, D02, P02 |
| Higher volume needed | 126 (50) | D01, D02, P02 |
| Standard payment term ("our standard Zahlungsziel is N days") | 126 (64) | P02, D02, P11 |
| Cash, financing, margin | 58 (31) | D02, P11, P02 |
| Final or limit stance | 116 (101) | D01, D02, P05 |
| Capacity (busy, overtime, fully booked) | 42 (26) | D02 DEMO-J1, P05 70250 |
| Management or committee approval | 47 (31) | D02 DEMO-C1, P03 70530 |
| Rival quote dismissed ("does not concern this part") | 33 (26) | D02, P05 70240, P01 70110 |
| Frozen prices (group directive) | 11 (3) | P03 70530 only |

**4. Our wording and the reactions**

- Negative: "What would you need from us to move further on the price?" (96 e-mails) drew "You asked what we need... you keep asking, I keep telling you: volume!" in P05 70210, 70240 and 70250. P05 ended with final_offer in 10 threads.
- Negative: "our order volume is fixed... we cannot commit to a higher volume" (P02 Nordmark, P03, P04, P05, D01). In P02 it became "as you cannot commit... our flexibility is strictly limited" and P02 b85685a5 walked at round 4. In D01 212404b7 it became "we have no room left... final offer" and then walked at round 6.
- Negative: "Could you confirm how long it remains valid?" (P10, P05 final rounds) drew "like I wrote in my last mail, the offer is valid for 14 days". Not a strong signal.
- Negative: P11 70140 ignored faster payment. Reactions: "I keep asking for faster payment... you just ignore it" (2 e-mails), then final_offer in 6 threads.
- Negative: sandbox urgency ("you need to close quickly") drew "I understand... However... our price remains" (D01 540adf42). Four e-mails, so weak evidence.
- Positive: citing a data point the supplier had not considered drew "We did not know that - a fair point" (P01 70110, 17 e-mails) and "Hallo, fair point on the electricity and the delivery score, you did your homework" (P05 70210 12116e91, round 1). The next price cut was 36.00 to 32.00.
- Mixed: our data citations drew "We checked the X data you cited; it holds and we took it into account" (about 145 sentences) or "it holds, but it does not change our calculation" (about 80 sentences; price history, delivery, volume).

**5. Warning signs before final_offer or walked_away** (last supplier e-mail before the first final_offer; practice threads and D01 and D02 sandbox)

| Case | Final-offer threads | Warning in the prior e-mail |
|---|---|---|
| D01 (DEMO-F1) | 36 | Prior status always open. Volume demand in 14, "we hold our offer" or "offer has not changed" in 12, "valid 30 days" in all 36 |
| D02 (DEMO-C1, DEMO-J1) | 16 | Cash or faster payment in 11, capacity or overtime in 7, standard term in 6 |
| P05 (70210, 70240, 70250) | 10 | "You keep asking what I need... volume!", "I cannot drop below", "tell me what volume you can commit to, or we stay at" |
| P10 (70410) | 6 | Volume-only price; "we checked the delivery record data... does not change our calculation". Walked after our timeout (a96b17ff) |
| P11 (70140) | 6 | "I keep asking for faster payment... you ignore it"; "if you can't give us better payment terms we have to hold" |
| P18 (70740) | 6 | "We must hold firm... absolute limit"; index clause mandatory |
| P02 (70510) | 6 | "Our flexibility is strictly limited", "you cannot commit to a higher volume" |
| P07, P08 | 5 each | "Would need a commitment to higher volumes or a longer contract"; index clause mandatory |
| P01, P03, P04 | 2 each | Volume demand or frozen prices |

Walk-aways: P02 b85685a5 (round 4, after our 362.93 counter, "general terms dictate this position"); P10 a96b17ff (after our final-offer timeout); D01 212404b7 (round 6, after our "volume is fixed" line).
